raw_response:
Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46 chromosomes. This is a diploid number, meaning that each cell in the body contains two sets of chromosomes, one inherited from each parent.

Source: National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI) [1]

Confidence level: High

Note: The Human Genome Project, a major international research effort, was completed in 2003 and confirmed the human genome to have 46 chromosomes, consisting of 22 pairs of autosomes (non-sex chromosomes) and one pair of sex chromosomes (X or Y). [1]

References:

[1] National Human Genome Research Institute. (2020). Understanding Your Genes. Retrieved from <https://www.genome.gov/genetics-family-health/understanding-genetic-tests-and-tests-results/>
